description: 🚀 We are AstroVibes, a team of aspiring AI developers and tech enthusiasts passionate about space exploration and innovation. Our interests include AI, Python, web development, and data analysis. We aim to build smart solutions for astronaut health monitoring. We welcome creative and motivated teammates with skills in AI/ML, Python, frontend development, UI/UX, healthcare research, or data science. Beginners are welcome too!
summary:
ASTROCARE AI is a live health monitoring system that lets an astronaut
evaluate their own health during a space mission. It tracks heart rate,
blood oxygen, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep and activity,
compares every reading with the astronaut's own baseline, and explains
every flag — the rule, the value, the threshold and the next step. An AI
health assistant answers questions using only real stored readings and
never invents a measurement. The system is live now at
https://astrocare-ai.ai.studio, with no login required. The github repo is https://github.com/abdul-hannan-official/Astrocare-ai.git.
details:
THE PROBLEM
An astronaut far from Earth must judge their own health. A single
reading can look normal while health is quietly drifting — heart rate,
oxygen, blood pressure, sleep and temperature shift a little each day.
On the way to Mars a reply from Earth can take 20–44 minutes, so the
crew cannot wait for ground control to notice. Months of vitals, sleep
and activity data pile up, and the warning gets buried.

OUR SOLUTION
ASTROCARE AI is a full-stack web app that answers one question for the
astronaut: how am I doing right now? It has six views: a Dashboard with
six vital-sign cards and a 24-hour telemetry trend; a Live Monitor where
a new reading is logged, validated and analysed (an impossible heart
rate of 300 is rejected outright); a Risk & Alerts centre with
explainable LOW / MODERATE / HIGH risk levels, each showing the exact
triggering measurements, deviations and recommended next steps; an AI
Health Assistant that answers in plain English from stored readings
only; Analytics with 24-hour trends, 7-day history, sleep statistics
and one-click CSV export; and a NASA Sources page linking the real
NASA resources behind the project.

HOW IT WORKS
Live simulated telemetry arrives every few seconds, or a reading is
entered manually. An Express API validates every value, stores it in
SQLite, and runs an explainable risk engine that checks both fixed
thresholds and the astronaut's rolling baseline — a drift from your own
normal is the early warning. Risk levels carry the reason, the numbers
and the next action, so a decision takes seconds. Missing data is
reported as missing; the system never guesses and never diagnoses.

VERIFIED WORKING
The live app was fully tested on 15 November 2026: all six views pass,
no login is required, no page errors. A test reading was saved and
appeared in the log, invalid input was rejected, the HIGH alert (SpO2
90.6%, heart rate 119, blood pressure 148/92 — seven deviations) fires
correctly with "Immediate assessment required", and the assistant's
answers use only real stored numbers. The demo video is a real screen
recording of the live app, not a mock-up.

TECHNOLOGY
React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS frontend, Express + SQLite backend,
Google Gemini powering the AI assistant with a grounded deterministic
fallback when no API key is set. The demo astronaut is Alex Morgan
(ORBIT-04), a fictional crew member on a simulated 180-day LEO
endurance mission, Day 47.

HONEST LIMITS
All demo readings are realistic simulated data, clearly labelled in the
app. The system is a research prototype: not a medical device, not
clinically validated, and not endorsed by NASA. Suggested indicators
not yet covered are blood sugar and mood tracking.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
